A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 16 pages of each were inspected, including equations, proofs and references; neither contains a separate appendix. Rendered pages resolve the mathematical symbols omitted by text extraction.

before.justification: v5 reports algorithms, theoretical regret bounds and proofs, but no original experimental, simulation, user-study or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v6 reports theoretical results only. Inspection of the complete PDF establishes that no original empirical outcomes are reported.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same master-base OMD procedures, regularizers, loss estimators and learning-rate updates.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical training/evaluation tasks. No tested domain or scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical comparator evaluations. The theoretical regret comparisons with EXP3.S and BOB are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental evaluation protocols. No splits, empirical metrics, training budgets or testing procedures are added or revised.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies or case studies. The existing theoretical analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical tests. The unchanged estimator-variance analysis is theoretical, rather than empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries appear in either version. The regret bounds and comparative findings reported for both algorithms remain identical.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, Section 2.1 lower bound, Theorems 1 and 2, Lemmas 1–4, and their derivations and proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: two OMD algorithms for an unknown switching parameter, with identical regret guarantees.

C2.justification: The explanations of estimator variance and clipping, stochastic-bandit applicability in Remark 2, and unresolved optimal worst-case regret in the conclusion are unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm initializations, parameter formulas and Remark 1's implementation guidance on OMD updates and clipping are unchanged. No code or data access information is added.

R1.justification: Cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Daniely et al. (2015) and Foster et al. (2020) move from page 15 to page 16; neither is added or removed.

P1.justification: v6 adds Section 5, Acknowledgment, thanking Joe Suk for helpful discussions, and updates the first-page arXiv version/date stamp. The research prose and existing section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment block shifts the References heading downward on page 15 and moves two bibliography entries onto page 16. The algorithm displays and remaining page layouts are retained.

improvement.justification: v6 adds an acknowledgment; the remaining differences are the version stamp and bibliography reflow. The methods, proofs, claims and implementation guidance are unchanged, with no meaningful net effect on the paper's rigor, completeness or clarity.
